parts.text: A student investigates the cooling of hot water in a beaker. The apparatus is shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student uses a thermometer to measure room temperature θ R . Room temperature is 22 °C. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student pours 100 cm 3 of hot water into an empty beaker. She records the temperature θ of the hot water in the V = 100 cm 3 row of Table 2.1, as shown. Without delay, she pours 20 cm 3 of cold water into the beaker. She stirs the water and measures the temperature of the mixture of hot and cold water. She repeats the procedure until she has added a total of 100 cm 3 of cold water to the beaker. All the readings are shown in Table 2.1. V is the total volume of water in the beaker. Complete the column headings in Table 2.1. [1] Table 2.1 V / θ / 100 87 120 73 140 65 160 59 180 54 200 49

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of temperature θ (y-axis) against total volume of water V (x-axis). You do not need to start the axes at the origin (0, 0). Draw the best-fit curve. [4]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
axes correctly labelled with quantity AND unit AND right way round
suitable scales (occupying at least ½ the grid)
plots correct to ± ½ small square AND precise plots
good best-fit line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) In the experiment, the student aims to investigate the effect on the temperature of the hot water as cold water is added.

ms.label: 2(d)(i)
ms.text: so that temperature change is due to cold water added rather than heat losses to the surroundings

ms.label: 2(d)(ii)
ms.text: to ensure even / constant temperature (throughout the liquid)

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text:
any two from:

•
